query: is tsukiji market a tourist trap
ai_overview:
Yes, the Tsukiji Outer Market has many elements of a tourist trap, though it is still a functioning market with genuine history and high-quality food. 
Reddit
·r/JapanTravelTips
 +1
Why People Call It a Tourist Trap
Inflated Prices: Since the famous wholesale inner market moved to Toyosu, the outer market has leaned heavily into tourism. Items like Wagyu skewers, uni (sea urchin) cups, and full sushi sets often carry heavily marked-up prices compared to standard neighborhood spots in Tokyo. 
YouTube
·Ninja Monkey
 +3
Extreme Crowds: The narrow alleys are constantly "rammed packed" and have been officially flagged by authorities for overtourism, making it hard to walk or eat comfortably. 
Reddit
·r/JapanTravelTips
 +1
Hit-or-Miss Quality: Some high-profile stalls with massive lines serve average or overpriced seafood because they rely on passing foot traffic rather than repeat local customers. 
Instagram
·grace chin
 +1
Why It Is Still Worth Visiting (If Done Right)
The Atmosphere: The sensory overload—sizzling charcoal grills, fresh fish blocks, knife shops, and street-food theatrics—gives it an energetic vibe you won't find easily elsewhere. 
Cheap Snacks Exist: You don't have to spend a fortune. Small, traditional items like freshly cooked tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelet) on a stick for a few hundred yen are still great value. 
Instagram
·the_undercover_food_critic
 +1
Timing & Alternatives:
Timing: Go early (right around 9:00 AM) before the midday crowds peak, and avoid Sundays, public holidays, and some Wednesdays when many shops close.
Alternatives: Check out nearby commercial zones like Tsukiji Uogashi or look for smaller, quieter vendor stalls tucked away from the main tourist paths where locals and working chefs still shop.
